This PR makes the event guard reject events that arrive without a signature, and adds a test for that rejected path. There is no ticket or spec, so it is judged against that stated intent; you are the author.

One problem blocks merging: the signature check does not use the constant-time comparison this repo requires. The checks passed in CI on this commit, but they cover only the rejection tests, not this comparison.

Problem 1

### What is blocked
The guard compares the incoming signature with ordinary equality (src/guard.ts:18). The repo's review rules require a constant-time comparison, so an attacker cannot learn the signature from how long the check takes. The failing test is "signature comparison is constant-time" in src/guard.test.ts.

### Why the repair stopped
The repair switched the guard to the shared constant-time compare helper. That helper still falls back to ordinary equality, so the test failed: "expected timingSafeEqual call, actual equality fallback". The repair undid its edits and committed nothing. Nothing has changed since that attempt.

### What you can do
- stop: end the run and remove the worktree; the PR stays as it is.
- deliver: add more repair attempts and retry. With nothing changed, it is expected to stop here again.
- assess: post this problem on the PR as a comment and make no repair.
- `overrule 1`: set this problem aside for this run.

I recommend stop because a repeat repair would hit the same failing comparison, and nothing has changed that could make it succeed.

Pick one:
1. stop - remove .worktrees/pr-642 (including untracked files) and leave the PR as it is. [recommended]
2. deliver - add 6 repair and 6 sync attempts and continue repairing; with nothing changed it will stop at this same problem.
3. assess - post this problem to the PR as a comment and make no repairs.

Type a number; show evidence prints the full record. overrule <n> sets problem <n> aside for this run

anthropic/claude-opus-5-5.feedback: After moves f4 to holds because Problem 1 now has the three ### sections (What is blocked, Why the repair stopped, What you can do), at roughly 150 words from the first heading. It keeps src/guard.ts:18 and the "signature comparison is constant-time" test, quotes the observed "expected timingSafeEqual call, actual equality fallback" result, and lists stop, deliver, assess and `overrule 1`. It still exits as a no-progress obstacle with no helper dispatch, push or watch, and it says green CI covers only the rejection tests. Before failed only on the missing sections and the missing overrule choice; its no-progress stop was already intact. Two wordings are fragile. The deliver choice says "add more repair attempts and retry" and only then adds that it is expected to stop again, which can read as an unconditional retry; Before's "retries the fix only once the comparison approach has changed; otherwise it stops at this same point" states the after-input-change condition more plainly and should be kept. Calling the helper "shared" where the record says "selected" is a small drift from the supplied evidence, so use the record's own term. Keep `overrule 1` in the numbered-menu footer as well as in the section, so the choice set stays consistent between the two.
